summary:
**Overall: 8.8/10.** This is a substantial improvement over the rejected native UI and clearly resembles the web reference. I would not yet award 9.

| Category | Score |
|---|---:|
| Hierarchy and web similarity | 9.1 |
| Proportions and space usage | 8.2 |
| Charcoal/glass surfaces | 9.2 |
| Typography | 9.0 |
| Thumbnails and queue | 9.0 |
| Controls and discoverability | 9.0 |
| Responsiveness | 8.5 |

I inspected actual desktop, compact, Stage, and belowfold PNGs alongside both reference images. The thumbnail queue, selected-row treatment, Video/Focus switch, white transport controls, and shuffle panel now communicate the same product as the web interface. The player and transport fit in the supplied initial viewports. Stage has a clear exit, and “Stop & close” is understandable.

Two remaining findings:

1. **The height cap leaves the video noticeably undersized inside a wide card.** At 760×680, the video is approximately 402 points wide inside a 720-point deck; at 1100×720, it is 473 inside 732. The compact and Stage captures consequently have broad empty shoulders around the media. This is geometrically correct, but less balanced than the reference’s near-full-width video. The fixed 276-point deck overhead and viewport subtraction cause this: [NativeUIStyle.swift:123](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffle/App/NativeUIStyle.swift:123). **Necessary refinement:** reduce vertical chrome and spacing in short windows so the exact 16:9 video can grow while transport remains visible. Preserve the corrected aspect ratio.

2. **The measurement artifact mixes initial and scrolled states.** `measurements.json` records the two paused belowfold cases after scrolling: their deck Y is −382, whereas their named initial screenshots show the deck onscreen. The rendering test appends measurements after producing the lower capture in [NativeUIRenderingTests.swift](/Users/gustavocaiano/.t3/worktrees/tubeshuffle/t3-310b873b/macos/TubeShuffleTests/Domain/Library/NativeUIRenderingTests.swift). **Necessary evidence fix:** snapshot initial bounds before scrolling and record belowfold bounds separately. This does not invalidate the earlier geometry assertions, but makes the exported evidence misleading.

The four previous findings appear addressed in the inspected source and captures. Compact Queue/Shuffle navigation is explicit, although I did not interactively exercise those buttons.

Limits: this was read-only source and image review; I did not rerun tests or exercise playback. Static WKWebView artwork and synthetic paused events establish layout evidence, not live YouTube playback, audio, OS controls, or policy acceptance. Those missing manual checks did **not** reduce the visual score. No files were edited.
